title: Calibration run manager & artifact governance: lineage, dedupe, tiered retention, and access model
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Build a durable, auditable, and cost-aware orchestration layer in Redwood Console for quantization calibration runs (FP8/INT8), their artifacts, and accuracy validation results. This ticket scopes the product requirements and acceptance criteria for a "run manager" that tracks run lineage, performs artifact deduplication, exposes tiered retention/archival policies, and enforces permissioning for access and downloads.

Background: Calibration jobs produce multiple artifacts (calibration histograms, activation distributions, quant profiles, eval reports). Customers need: reproducible run lineage, cheap long-term storage for old artifacts, fast access for recent runs, and fine-grained permissions for audit/regulatory workflows. Current state: artifacts are stored in S3 buckets ad-hoc, no consistent retention policy, limited UI visibility into run parentage, and no standardized checksum/dedupe leading to duplicate storage and confusing UX.

Scope: product UX and API surface for run lifecycle; metadata model for runs (id, parent_run_id, model_version, dataset_hash, seed, status); artifact metadata (type, checksum, size, storage_tier); retention and archival policy UI; RBAC mapping for artifact access (team-level, project-level, manual exceptions); integration points for accuracy validation harness and diff-based regression alerts.

Out of scope for this ticket: changes to low-level backend kernel quantization algorithms, model compilers, or new storage backends beyond S3/GCS abstraction. Separate engineering tickets will handle expensive re-quant pipelines and local on-prem storage adapters.

Constraints & trade-offs: 1) Cost vs. discoverability — keep metadata in our DB for efficient listing but offload large blobs to customer-owned buckets or long-term cold storage. 2) Consistency vs. speed — we will allow eventual consistency for artifact ingestion to reduce latency on heavy runs, but provide visibility and retry UX in Console. 3) Deduplication expectations — we will dedupe based on content checksums and artifact fingerprinting; preserve original run->artifact mapping for audit even if object deduped.

User personas: ML platform engineers running large calibration sweeps, model owners validating regression on quant profiles, security/compliance reviewers auditing artifact access, and cost-conscious infra owners who want tiered archival controls.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI: Run detail page shows lineage (parent/child runs), artifacts, checksums, storage tier, and last-accessed timestamp
Artifact dedupe: identical artifact blobs are stored once (same checksum) and Console links multiple run artifacts to the canonical store object
Retention policy: Admins can set default project-level retention (e.g., 30d hot, 365d warm, archive/cold) and override per-run with justification
Permissions: RBAC enforced for artifact view/download; audit logs record user, action, artifact id, timestamp, and originating run
APIs: Public REST endpoints to create run, attach artifacts with metadata (checksum,size,type), list runs with lineage, and update retention policy
Accuracy validation: Console displays pass/fail and delta metrics for candidate vs baseline quant profiles and links to evaluation artifacts
Migration: Existing artifacts are identified by checksum and re-linked to new metadata model without duplicating objects when possible
Performance: Listing run with <=100 artifacts returns in <500ms for typical project scale (1000 runs)
tasks: Write PRD that defines run + artifact metadata schema and examples
Design Console wireframes: run list, run detail, artifact viewer, retention settings modal
Backend: API endpoints for run lifecycle, artifact attach/dedup, retention policy enforcement
Storage: implement checksum-based dedup layer and storage-tier metadata (hot/warm/cold)
RBAC: map Console roles to artifact permissions; integrate with existing SSO/SAML groups
Accuracy validation integration: display diffs, thresholds, and regression alerts in run view
Migration script: scan legacy buckets, compute checksums, and backfill metadata with idempotency
E2E tests: ingestion, dedupe, retention TTL job, RBAC enforcement, audit log entries
Docs: Console help page, API docs, and migration guide for customers
Rollout: staged enablement (internal -> beta customers -> general availability)
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ava Martinez: Kickoff meeting notes: Eng raised concerns about checksum compute cost for very large artifacts; suggested sampling strategy and a fast rolling hash for initial detection. Action: ENG to prototype rolling-hash + full-checksum flow.

2025-02-20 - Priya Kulkarni (Engineering): Prototype results: rolling-hash reduces full checksum invocations by ~78% on our calibration corpus. We need to 1) define collision handling and 2) measure CPU cost on batch nodes. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/248

2025-02-25 - Miguel Santos (Design): Uploaded wireframes for run detail page and retention modal: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/calibration-run-manager-v1. UX call scheduled 2025-02-27 to review edge cases (multi-tenant visibility and blocked downloads).

2025-02-28 - Ethan Zhao (Assignee): Decided to keep artifact objects immutable. Dedup will create a canonical object and maintain run->artifact pointers; deletion will be via retention TTL and will only remove canonical object when no run references remain. Impact: slightly more complex GC but simpler audit trails.

2025-03-03 - Security review (L. Chen): Request: encryption-at-rest with KMS key per-organization for cold archive; also require export approval workflow for sensitive artifacts. Logged as dependency on ENG-4380.
2025-03-04 - Product review (Ava Martinez): Updated acceptance criteria to include listing performance and migration idempotency. Added customer-facing copy for retention justification prompt.
